result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers clearly say to keep the identity. B does better at naming what already works, including the black version, and at saying what would justify a rebrand (the mark misleads, fails at small sizes, gets confused with a rival, or the store expands). B's suggestions then grow into a full version set, a custom letter detail, a second color and a supporting typeface, which edges toward a redesign. A stays tighter and limits itself to clean vectors, spacing, a locked orange value and an optional monogram. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers clearly say to keep the identity, and both explain why a generic sans with a gradient would not solve a real problem. B keeps its changes smaller (redraw cleanly, lock the orange, keep it consistent, add an optional monogram) and asks for concrete evidence of lost business. A goes further than small refinements: it adds a custom letter detail, a full matrix of versions, a second color and a supporting typeface, though it does credit the black one-color version more explicitly.
